title: Attribution Guard Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan · #315 the attribution guard misses gh api and curl
approval: Build plan approved: attribution guard gaps

short.lead: The design you approved is split into four sub-issues of #315, built in order on the branch AjsAgent/issue-315-attribution-routes, which starts from main. A builder helper does each step, one at a time, and each step ends with verify.py passing. The design is written up in docs/4-systems/guards.md under "Credit on GitHub", and the decision is logged.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it builds and when it is done.
items: #316: check gh api and curl writes, and bodies in files

The guard now also checks the five gh api write routes (create a pull request, create an issue, edit an issue, comment with a body file, pull request with --input) and curl, and reads -F body=@file and --input file. A plain gh api read is not checked.
Two new text patterns catch the "Generated by Claude Code" footer, with or without a trailing slash on its link.
#318: read the body back after opening
A PostToolUse hook fetches the new pull request or issue once and tells me if a footer is on it. A failed fetch says it could not check.
The rule says the "with Claude" badge and the footer can't be removed from a cloud session, and the version goes up one patch.
I open the pull request and hand it over with a QA page. You open one pull request from a cloud session and compare what the read-back reported with what GitHub shows on the pull request.
Test, then pass or fail it.

changes: The credit check and one new PostToolUse hook.
The credit check sees git commit, gh pr and gh issue only.
It also sees the five gh api write routes and curl, and the created body is read back.
New cases: one for each of the five gh api routes and curl, two for the footer, and three for the read-back's outcomes.
No case for any gh api or curl route.
A case for each, so a regression fails the suite.
The read-back cases stub the network call.

wrapup.summary: Four sub-issues of #315, built in order by a builder helper, each ending with verify.py passing.
wrapup.changing: The credit check in hook.py, one new hook, verify.py, the rule text and the version.
wrapup.next: I build #316 first, then #317, #318 and #319, then open the pull request with a QA page.
